extracted.intended_audience: Navy (and other DoD) contracting officers, procurement staff, and Task Group members involved in CITA / A-76 service procurements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Contracting Officers and Task Groups on planning, organizing, communicating, staffing, and administering service procurements under the CITA / A-76 procedures, including SOW development, cost comparison, milestone planning, and interaction with interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of consolidated packages / combining functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The various activities for which the contracting office has procurement authority should jointly review their requirements and prepare consolidated packages for submission to the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the Contracting Officer participating in or even taking the lead in the planning effort, it might be possible to coordinate an overall plan for orderly processing of various consolidated packages throughout any one fiscal year. Lack of coordination leads to varied work statements and hinders preparation of larger solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work Statement consistency and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Work statements varied from acceptable to poor; there was often little similarity between work statements submitted from different activities for the same service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly prepared or inconsistent SOWs will hinder consolidated solicitations. Contracting offices should assist requiring activities in developing acceptable, standardized SOWs suitable for solicitation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with interested groups — avoid premature statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer must insure that he makes no statements that would seem to indicate a decision has been reached on any areas that require approval by a higher authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CITA is a sensitive area; Congress and other stakeholders must be kept advised of status. Awareness of content and spirit of communication guidance can preclude command embarrassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of decision authority when involved in Assessment Phase
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Contracting Officer is involved in any way in the Assessment Phase of the CITA program he must realize that the ultimate decision as to what will be included in a particular inventory cycle is not made at the local command level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting personnel should avoid implying local final authority and should coordinate communications accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA responses: coordinate with legal counsel and higher authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Inputs to replies to Freedom of Information Act requests should be prepared in close concert with legal counsel and advice or assistance should be sought from higher authority if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large multipart FOIA requests (e.g., over thirty questions requiring extensive documentation) require legal review before response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to union and public inquiries: consistency, accuracy, and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to inquiries from union employees affected under the CITA program should be consistent, accurate and supportive of the general policy. Requests for written responses should be coordinated with the Naval Supply Systems Command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the final analysis, replies to public inquiries remain the responsibility of the field activity; coordinate for consistency and accuracy to avoid mixed messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CBD notice to determine non-availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing guidance mandates at a minimum the use of a CBD notice in determining the non-availability of commercial concerns to perform the desired service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBD notice is the minimum action; several related questions remain unanswered and require Contracting Officer judgment and possibly higher-level guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation/leadership in multi-functional solicitation development
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in the development of multi-functional solicitations and consolidation into one solicitation document of the same function for different activities are areas in which the Contracting Officer may provide assistance and professional advice; he can sometimes take the lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active contracting-office involvement reduces risk of poor SOWs and ill-defined milestones; reluctance to participate often leads to inferior solicitation packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational review and potential reorganization to support program
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should examine long-term internal organization and staffing and consider reorganization to more fully support the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include establishing a CITA program coordinator, a dedicated Services Branch, or a separate Contract Administration Branch; feasibility varies by activity and geographic dispersion of customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of cradle-to-grave vs. dedicated contract administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The cradle-to-grave philosophy (negotiator retains responsibility through administration) versus creating a dedicated Contract Administration Branch is a tradeoff to be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cradle-to-grave enhances continuity and familiarization with acquisition process, but dedicated contract administration can prevent administration from slipping when negotiators face backlogs. The Air Force example shows dedicated administration supports pre-performance conferences, daily work plans, periodic progress meetings, and surveillance planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish billets for procurement oversight at receiving activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement could be levied on activities engaged in significant contracting-out to establish a billet for a procurement series person to oversee contract administration and assist in SOW preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One person per given dollar value of contracts is recommended; training for these personnel is generally provided by the contracting office. As program grows, additional billets may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate workload impact and plan (query customers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should plan for possible significant increases in CITA purchase requests (e.g., over 45 functions in FY80 and 115+ over FY80-82) and query customers to estimate probable number and type of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a planning aid, requesting input from customers about likely submissions is prudent and helps schedule resources and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT) as performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: PALT is defined as the time to process a purchase request from receipt in the contracting office until award; the formal goal for actions in excess of $10,000 is 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CITA-related procurements often exceed this goal; close adherence to milestones and Contracting Officer personal monitoring are essential to avoid long delays. Examples showed 169 and 224 day cycles due to SOW development, solicitation method, and SBA negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage offer acceptance periods and mitigate expiration risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerers may have acceptance periods (e.g., 60 days) that can expire during long procurements; contracting officers should seek longer acceptance periods (perhaps 75 to 90 days) and adhere to milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acceptance period expires and offerers withdraw, resolicitation or restart may be necessary; active milestone adherence and monitoring help avoid this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on contracting authority (NAVSUP vs NAVFAC) and use of predominant user
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine which command (e.g., NAVSUP or NAVFAC) will provide contracting expertise for given functional categories; for multi-function contracting, the concept of predominant user will determine who will procure the needed service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAVSUP was to issue a listing indicating procurement responsibility; unresolved authority can delay actions such as resolicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on A-76 procedures and role limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel need at minimum an overview of the cost comparison process; the Contracting Officer should be familiar with his role but excluded from areas (e.g., developing Government cost estimates) where guidance says he should not participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A four-day course exists (Army Logistics Management Center) but is oriented to financial management personnel. More appropriate would be a dedicated in-house program tailored to current guidance and the Contracting Officer's Task Group role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group composition, milestones, and central duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Task Group usually includes representatives from the functional organization, manpower/personnel, finance/accounting, legal, and contracting; the group must establish realistic milestones and drive the cost comparison process to completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary activities: prepare comprehensive SOW, develop accurate Government cost estimate, conduct cost comparison once offers received, prepare Decision Summary Recommendations for Approving Authority. Success depends on early communications, detailed planning, and diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Task Group role: chairperson duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairs all meetings; oversees preparation of the in-house Government cost estimate; maintains objectivity and integrity of the system; establishes and monitors milestones; provides guidance on preparation of SOW; attends pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences; prepares and forwards Decision Summary Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairperson may be from functional organization or comptroller/planning officer depending on service; role is central to maintaining schedule and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Task Group role: manpower/personnel office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifies labor/union representatives of the study; identifies Government positions affected by study; prepares possible Reduction in Force plans; takes action to assist displaced Government employees including possible hiring by contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manpower office actions are crucial to address labor impacts and union communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Task Group role: functional office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Develops and prepares the Statement of Work; identifies Government Furnished Material to be provided to contractor; develops the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional office is primarily responsible for the technical content and surveillance approach of the future contract; poor SOWs here cause downstream delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Task Group role: comptroller/financial office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepares Government Cost Estimate and conducts the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial personnel develop cost models and perform comparisons; Contracting Officer should not draft the Government cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Task Group role: legal office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews SOW and solicitation for legal sufficiency; assists in responses to FOIA requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal review is required for FOIA inputs and to ensure solicitation documents are legally sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Task Group role: contracting office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Assures contracting milestones are met; reviews work specifications; solicits bids/offers from private industry; conducts pre-bid or proposal conferences; explains cost procedures in conjunction with the requiring activity; presides at bid openings and determines successful responsive/responsible bids or acceptable/responsible offers; awards contracts; notifies officials when a contract is awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting office must be sufficiently involved early to avoid poorly prepared SOWs and ill-defined milestones, and to maintain the integrity of the competitive bidding system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone planning and adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Task Group members must establish realistic milestones and strive to meet these deadlines (e.g., SOW completion, Government cost estimate, cost comparison, Decision Summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit example and narrative emphasize that adherence to schedule and personal monitoring by Contracting Officer are essential; lack of milestones or failure to meet them causes excessive PALT and potential loss of offerers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-performance conferences and active contract surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling and approval of pre-performance conferences, daily work plans, periodic progress meetings, and similar post-award considerations are recommended to ensure Government receives entitled services and to surface problems early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air Force practice requires such planning; Navy offices without dedicated administration often performed little planning leading to surveillance gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide period base for cost comparison and treatment of options
rubrics_metrics.description: There is confusion regarding the use of options and whether the cost comparison will be based on a one-year or a three-year period; this must be decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period chosen affects cost estimates and comparisons; clarify early in Task Group planning to avoid rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for evaluating cost-type and incentive proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel must understand methodologies for evaluating cost-type proposals (e.g., cost-plus-award-fee) in comparison to in-house cost estimates; incorrect assumptions (minimum vs maximum performance levels) are common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and written guidance are necessary; both 'minimum' and 'maximum' approaches were cited as incorrect by interviewees, indicating a need for correct evaluative methodology (details addressed elsewhere in guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up procedures when Government estimate is lower than private offers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Government cost estimate is lower than that offered by the private sector, the requirement should be resolicited using Small Business Restricted Advertising or unrestricted methods, in accordance with existing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays in processing resolicitations (e.g., pending NAVFAC release) can stall award; ensure contracting authority and procedures are clear before reselection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of reliance on DCAS for contract administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegation of contract administration to DCAS provided little additional assistance in CITA contracts except for renegotiating wage agreements; dependence on DCAS may be insufficient for significant contract administration problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting offices should not assume DCAS can handle substantial contract administration tasks and should plan staffing accordingly.
